response.sql: WITH item_stats AS (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(product_price * 1.0 / NULLIF(derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, AVG(line_item_count) AS avg_line_item_count FROM item_stats;

assumptions.assumption: A line item's ratio is missing when product_price or derived_total_cost is NULL, or when derived_total_cost is 0 (NULLIF turns it into NULL). Those ratios are skipped in the per-item average.
The per-item line-item count includes every invoice line item for that order item, including items whose ratios are all missing. The request only says to skip missing ratios when averaging ratios.
An order item whose ratios are all missing has a NULL average ratio, so it is excluded from the outer average of ratios but still counted in the outer average of counts.

alternatives.interpretation: Average the line-item counts only over order items that have at least one valid ratio, so items with no usable ratio are excluded from both outer averages.
alternatives.sql: WITH item_stats AS (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(product_price * 1.0 / NULLIF(derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, AVG(CASE WHEN avg_ratio IS NOT NULL THEN line_item_count END) AS avg_line_item_count FROM item_stats;
